//: Filled into every page by scripts/build-site.mjs. The build FAILS while legalName or jurisdiction is empty, so half-finished legal pages cannot reach the live site — same guard as config.js's API_BASE.
//legalName: Your full legal name. Paddle's domain review wants the sole trader's legal name in the Terms, not just a brand. Trading as 'Ad Interceptor' is fine alongside it.
//jurisdiction: Country (and state/province if relevant) whose law governs the Terms — where you are resident as a sole trader. e.g. 'India' or 'England and Wales'.
//webStoreUrl: Public Chrome Web Store listing for the LIVE build. The landing page had no install link at all until 2026-09-10, so the site described a product a reviewer could not obtain — a bad look in any merchant-of-record domain review. Pin the ID-ONLY form: the slug is derived from the listing TITLE, which is localised into 20 locales, so a slug URL is not stable. The bare id 301s to the canonical slug. The build refuses to run while this is empty.
//processorName: The PAYMENT PROCESSOR, not a merchant of record. This distinction is legally load-bearing and changed on 2026-09-12: Paddle and Dodo were both merchants of record, meaning THEY were the legal seller and owed the tax. Both declined the account over ad blocking. Going direct means the seller of record is legalName — the pages must say so, and the tax obligation is ours, not the processor's.
//dodoMode: 'test' or 'live'. Controls which checkout host the Get Pro button points at. Switching to live is a deliberate release step, not a default.
//dodoProductId: The Pro product in Dodo's catalogue. Goes straight into the static payment link. Empty = checkout unconfigured and the button says so.
//dodoCheckoutBase: Static payment link base. The page links here directly rather than loading a checkout SCRIPT, so the site now loads NO third-party resource at all — which is what the privacy policy claims. Confirm the TEST-mode host in the Dodo dashboard before flipping dodoMode; it is not documented publicly and must not be guessed.
//apiBase: Licence API origin, same value as config.js API_BASE. The success panel calls it to fetch the key by transaction id. Empty = checkout still works but the key must be issued by hand.
//salesEnabled: Master switch for the buy button, independent of paddleEnvironment. Keep FALSE until a PRO_ENABLED extension build is live in the Chrome Web Store. Selling before then hands buyers a licence key the published extension cannot activate: they pay and get nothing. The old gate keyed off sandbox mode, which silently stopped protecting anything the moment the config went to production.
